result:
The proposed answer is wrong. The solution confuses the cover ideal with the edge ideal when it checks $n=4$.

For $C_4$, the cover ideal is $J(C_4)=(x_1x_2,x_2x_3,x_3x_4,x_4x_1)=(x_1,x_3)\cap(x_2,x_4)$, not $(x_1x_3,x_2x_4)$. Since $C_4$ is bipartite, $J^{(t)}=J^t$, and because the two prime components use disjoint variables, $J^t=A\cap B$ with $A=(x_1,x_3)^t$ and $B=(x_2,x_4)^t$.

Take the short exact sequence $0\to S/(A\cap B)\to S/A\oplus S/B\to S/(A+B)\to 0$. Here $\operatorname{depth}S/A=\operatorname{depth}S/B=2$ and $\operatorname{depth}S/(A+B)=0$ for $t\ge 2$, since $(x_1,x_3)^t+(x_2,x_4)^t$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary in the variables $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ after tensoring the two Artinian pieces. The depth lemma then forces $\operatorname{depth}S/J(C_4)^t=1$.

The proposed formula $\lceil n/3\rceil$ gives $2$ at $n=4$, so it fails. The formula $\lceil (n-1)/3\rceil$ gives $1$ at $n=4$ and $1$ at $n=3$, which matches both checked cases. That is the form I recall from the literature on symbolic powers of cover ideals of cycles, though I have only verified it at $n=3$ and $n=4$.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
